cues.en: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome back David Crathwall. Good morning. It's Friday already. I don't know how that happened. We have a new record. Mark Johnson and Eric Soldin both wore ties the entire week. That's news. You know, yeah, I hear it. I hear it. That's the way I feel.
cues.zh: 女士们先生们，请欢迎David Crathwall回来。早上好。已经是周五了。我不知道怎么就这样了。我们有了新纪录。Mark Johnson和Eric Soldin整周都打着领带。这可是新闻。你知道，是的，我听到了。我听到了。我就是这种感觉。

cues.en: I'm with you. I have to tell you a little story this morning to introduce our special guest and I promise to make it short so I will. In 1979, I was a sixth grade teacher and I saw an Apple II and I had to have the Apple II so I bought one and took it home, started programming, which turns out was probably the most interesting thing you could do with a computer back in 1979. And it really changed my life.
cues.zh: 我同意你。今天早上我得讲个小故事来介绍我们的特别嘉宾，我保证会简短，所以我会的。1979年，我是一名六年级老师，我看到一台Apple II，我必须拥有那台Apple II，所以我买了一台带回家，开始编程，结果这可能是1979年用电脑能做的最有趣的事。它真的改变了我的生活。

cues.en: And about 10 years later, I found myself at Apple Computer, moved out from Boston and took a job out here. And I was out in the first week doing that sort of relocation thing and having dinner at a restaurant. My family was still in Boston. And I saw Steve Jobs across on the other side of the restaurant having dinner. And I thought, I really should just sort of walk over and interrupt his dinner.
cues.zh: 大约10年后，我发现自己在苹果电脑公司，从波士顿搬来，在这里找了份工作。第一周我在做那种搬家的事，在一家餐厅吃晚饭。我的家人还在波士顿。我看到Steve Jobs在餐厅另一边吃晚饭。我想，我真的应该走过去打断他的晚餐。

cues.en: tell him, you know, thank you and you know, you've changed my life. And I sort of thought about that for a while. I thought that's really rude. And it probably happens to him all the time. And I don't want to be like that. So I didn't do it. And in a way, I'm kind of glad that I hesitated because it gives me an opportunity to thank him this morning in a public setting among people who probably understand that better than anyone else on the planet. So it's a special pleasure this morning to introduce and thank
cues.zh: 告诉他，你知道，谢谢，你知道，你改变了我的生活。我想了一会儿。我觉得那真的很无礼。这可能一直发生在他身上。我不想那样。所以我没做。在某种程度上，我有点高兴我犹豫了，因为这给了我机会今天早上在公共场合感谢他，在可能比地球上任何人都更理解这一点的人中间。所以今天早上特别荣幸地介绍并感谢

cues.en: a person who has changed so many of our lives, Steve Jobs. I've had it. Thank you. You're welcome. Good morning. Thank you very much. I really appreciate that. And I really appreciate you not interrupting me for my dinner with what was hopefully a beautiful woman. I wanted to come and just have a chat this morning. I know you've been getting lots of presentations all week, so I didn't want to do a big fancy presentation.
cues.zh: 一个改变了我们这么多人生活的人，Steve Jobs。我受够了。谢谢。不客气。早上好。非常感谢。我真的很感激。我真的很感激你们没有打断我和一位希望是美丽女士的晚餐。今天早上我想来 just 聊聊。我知道你们整周都在听很多演讲，所以我不想做一个大而花哨的演讲。

cues.en: But what I want to do is just chat and so we get to spend 45 minutes or so together and I want to talk about whatever you want to talk about. I have opinions on most things so I figured if you just want to start asking some questions, we'll go to some good places. Just to set the tone a little bit, I'm actually pretty excited about the way things are going. I think that there are some really good people whom you met this week running
cues.zh: 不过我今天想做的就是聊聊天，所以我们能一起待上45分钟左右，我想聊你们想聊的任何话题。我对大多数事情都有自己的看法，所以我想，如果你们直接开始提问，我们就能聊到一些有意思的地方。先定个基调吧，其实我对事情的进展挺兴奋的。我觉得有一些非常优秀的人，你们这周已经见过了，他们现在掌管着

cues.en: the key areas of Apple now. And I think they're making enormous progress towards executing what is a pretty clear strategy. And that strategy revolves around one fundamental concept, which is to make some really great products. And I believe, very firmly, that there is still a very sizable market for some really great products. And there are some giant holes that we can fill with your help.
cues.zh: Apple的关键领域。而且我认为他们在执行一个相当清晰的战略方面正取得巨大进展。这个战略围绕一个基本理念，那就是做出一些真正伟大的产品。我坚信，真正伟大的产品仍有非常大的市场。而且有一些巨大的空白，我们可以在你们的帮助下填补。

cues.en: So I think we are embarked on a course to, after a hiatus of several years, turning this thing around to make some really good and unique products. We need a lot of software for them. That's where you come in. So I am open to entertaining any of your questions. And I hope you have some good ones this morning. What about OpenDoc? What about OpenDoc? Yeah. What about it? It's dead, right?
cues.zh: 所以我认为我们已经踏上了一条路，在中断了几年之后，要把这件事扭转过来，做出一些真正优秀且独特的产品。我们需要为它们开发大量软件。这就是你们发挥作用的地方。所以我愿意听取你们的任何问题。我希望今天早上你们能问出一些好问题。OpenDoc怎么样？OpenDoc怎么样？是啊。它怎么了？它已经死了，对吧？

cues.en: It's dead, right? Yeah. Well, let me say something that's sort of generic. I know some of you spent a lot of time working on stuff that we put a bullet in the head of. I apologize. I feel your pain. But Apple suffered for several years from lousy engineering management. I have to say it. And there were people...
cues.zh: 它已经死了，对吧？是啊。好吧，让我说点比较笼统的话。我知道你们中有些人花了很多时间在做那些被我们一枪毙掉的东西上。我道歉。我理解你们的痛苦。但Apple多年来一直受糟糕的工程管理之苦。我必须这么说。而且有些人在……

cues.en: that we're going off in 18 different directions doing arguably interesting things in each one of them. Good engineers, lousy management. And what happened was you look at the farm that's been created with all these different animals going in different directions and it doesn't add up. The total is less than the sum of the parts. And so we had to decide what are the fundamental directions we're going in and what makes sense and what doesn't.
cues.zh: 我们同时朝18个不同方向推进，每个方向做的事或许都挺有意思。工程师很优秀，管理层却糟糕透顶。结果就是，你看着这座农场，各种动物朝不同方向乱跑，整体根本不成体系。整体小于各部分之和。于是我们不得不决定，哪些才是我们真正要走的根本方向，哪些说得通，哪些说不通。

cues.en: And there were a bunch of things that didn't. And microcosmically, they might have made sense. Macrocosmically, they made no sense. And you know, the hardest thing is, when you think about focusing, right? You think, well, focusing is saying yes, no. Focusing is about saying no. Focusing is about saying no. And you've got to say no, no, no, no. And when you say no, you piss off people. And they go talk to the San Jose Mercury, and they write a shitty article about you. You know? And it's really a pisser.
cues.zh: 有很多方向是说不通的。从微观上看，它们或许说得通；从宏观上看，它们毫无意义。你知道，最难的是，想想“聚焦”这件事，对吧？你以为聚焦就是说“是”和“不”，其实聚焦就是说“不”。聚焦就是说“不”。你得不停地说不、不、不、不。而当你说不时，会得罪人。他们跑去跟《圣何塞水星报》说，然后人家就写一篇关于你的烂文章。你知道吗？这真让人窝火。

cues.en: Because you want to be nice, you don't want to tell the San Jose Mercury, the person that's telling you this, you know, just was asked to leave, or this or that, or this or that. So you take the lumps. And Apple's been taking their share of lumps for the last six months in a very unfair way. And it's been taking them, you know, like an adult. And I'm proud of that. And there's more to come, I'm sure. There's more to come. I mean, some of these, I read these articles about some of these people that have left. I know some of these people. They haven't done anything in seven years.
cues.zh: 因为你想做个好人，不想告诉《圣何塞水星报》，那个跟你说这事的人，其实是被请走的，或者这样那样。所以你只能忍气吞声。过去六个月，苹果一直以极不公平的方式承受着属于自己的那份指责。而且它一直像个成年人一样承受着。我为此感到骄傲。我确信，后面还有更多。还有更多。我是说，其中有些，我读过一些关于离职人员的文章。我认识其中一些人。他们七年里什么也没做成。

cues.en: And, you know, they leave and it's like, you know, it's like the company's gonna fall apart the next day. And so, you know, I think there'll be stories like that that come and go, but focus is about saying no. And the result of that focus is gonna be some really great products where the total is much greater than the sum of the parts. And OpenDoc, I mean, I was for putting a bullet in the head of OpenDoc. I didn't think it was great technology, but B, it didn't fit. The rest of the world isn't gonna use OpenDoc.
cues.zh: 他们一走，大家就觉得公司第二天就要垮了似的。所以我觉得这种八卦总是传一阵就过去，但“专注”的核心就是要懂得说不。而专注的成果，就是做出一些真正伟大的产品，其整体价值远大于各部分之和。至于 OpenDoc，我反正是主张直接给它一枪毙了的。一来我觉得它算不上多优秀的技术，二来，它根本不合时宜。世界上其他人根本不会去用 OpenDoc。

cues.en: And I think as a container strategy, there's some stuff in the Java space that's much better. And even the OpenDoc guys were basically trying to rewrite the whole thing in Java anyway, which was a restart. So it didn't make sense. Yes, sir. Steve, what do we do about the press? I mean, the Wall Street Journal reporters get up in the morning, sell Apple short, and then go write stories about us. And it's clear that it's a perception versus reality problem.
cues.zh: 而且我认为作为容器策略，Java 领域有些方案要好得多。甚至连 OpenDoc 团队自己本来就打算用 Java 彻底重写，这等于是推倒重来。所以继续做它根本毫无意义。请讲，先生。——Steve，我们该怎么应对媒体？我是说，《华尔街日报》的记者每天早上爬起来做空 Apple，接着就跑去写我们的报道。这显然是个认知与现实脱节的问题。

cues.en: They don't know shit about operating systems. They don't know anything about tools. They don't know what's going on in the future. They don't know that we're building icebergs and you build them from the bottom up. Sure. You know, I'm sure that a lot of you have had this experience where you're changing, you're growing as a person, and people still, people tend to treat you like you were 18 months ago.
cues.zh: 他们对操作系统屁都不懂。对开发工具也一窍不通。他们根本不知道未来会是怎样。他们不知道我们正在打造的是冰山，而冰山是要从水底自下而上构筑的。确实。我相信你们很多人都有过这种体会：你自身在改变、在成长，但别人还是习惯用你18个月前的老眼光来看待你。

cues.en: And it's really frustrating sometimes when you're growing up and you're becoming more capable and you've solved, maybe you had some personality quirks you've kind of gotten over, whatever it may be. And people still treat you like you were a year to 18 months ago. It can be very frustrating. Well, it's the same with a company. It's the same with the press. The press is going to have a lag time. And the best thing that we can do about the press is to embrace them, do the best we can to educate them about the strategy.
cues.zh: 有时候真的很让人沮丧，你在成长，能力在提升，也许你改掉了一些性格上的小毛病，不管是什么。但人们还是把你当成一年到一年半前的样子。这真的很让人沮丧。公司也是一样。媒体也是一样。媒体会有滞后。我们对媒体能做的最好的事就是接纳他们，尽我们所能让他们了解我们的战略。

cues.en: to keep our eye on the prize, and that is turning out some great products, communicating directly with our customers as best we can, getting the community of people that are gonna make this stuff successful like yourselves in the loop so you know everything, and just marching forward one foot in front of the other, and the press will take care of, it's like the stock price, the press and the stock price will take care of themselves. By the end of this year, it's gonna look quite different.
cues.zh: 紧盯目标，那就是做出伟大的产品，尽我们所能直接与客户沟通，让那些要推动这件事成功的人——比如你们——了解情况，知道一切，然后一步一步往前走，媒体会自己处理好的，就像股价一样，媒体和股价都会自己理顺。到今年年底，情况会大不一样。

cues.en: And I mean, I'm like an old man now in this industry, and I've seen the ups and downs. And when you see enough of them, you know that's going to happen. So when you get up in the morning and the press is selling Apple short, go out and buy some shares. That's what I would do. That's what I have done. Sir. Apple certainly has a tradition of introducing new technologies to become standards. But lately, Apple seems more apologetic about being different than it is proud about being different. And as a developer, you start to feel the same way.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，在这个行业里我现在算是个老人了，我见过起起落落。当你见得够多，你就知道这些事一定会发生。所以早上起来看到媒体在唱衰苹果，那就去买点股票。我会这么做。我也确实这么做过。先生。苹果确实有引入新技术并使之成为标准的传统。但最近，苹果似乎对自己与众不同更感到抱歉，而不是感到自豪。作为开发者，你也会开始有同样的感受。

cues.en: And I just wonder, you know, a few years after introducing the Macintosh, what applicant can do to get his balls back? Yeah. I got to tell you, I have a little different point of view on that. I think Apple's had its head in the sand for the last many years. Excuse me. There has been so much that's happened in terms of network computing, as an example.
cues.zh: 我不禁想问，在推出 Macintosh 几年之后，申请人要怎么做才能把自己的胆子找回来？是的。我得告诉你们，我对这件事有点不同的看法。我觉得苹果在过去很多年里一直把头埋在沙子里。不好意思。比如说，在网络计算方面发生了那么多事。

cues.en: that Apple's completely missed out on. The Mac is probably one of the least network computer communities in the world in terms of really making use of powerful networks. I mean, like when next joined Apple, right, next has an extremely sophisticated network infrastructure for doing network computing compared to Apple. And, you know, even now we struggle getting the Apple folks to understand it because the Mac has been
cues.zh: 而苹果完全错过了。就真正利用强大网络而言，Mac 大概是世界上网络化程度最低的计算机社区之一。我的意思是，比如 NeXT 加入苹果的时候，对吧，与苹果相比，NeXT 拥有极其成熟的网络基础设施来做网络计算。而且，你知道，即使现在我们也很难让苹果的人理解这一点，因为 Mac 一直

cues.en: because of all this proprietariness in every way, because of the attitude of arrogance that we can not only invent our own networking, but invent our own this, and invent our own that, and invent our own this, it's in its own little world. And the rest of the world with so much investments passed it by. And so we need to bring the MAC up into the modern world in many areas like network computing. And to do that, because we weren't first,
cues.zh: 因为各方面都这么封闭，因为那种傲慢的态度——我们不仅能发明自己的网络，还能发明自己的这个、发明自己的那个、发明自己的这个，它活在自己的小世界里。而世界上其他地方带着那么多投资从它身边超了过去。所以我们需要在很多领域把 Mac 带入现代世界，比如网络计算。要做到这一点，因为我们已经不是第一个了，

cues.en: Because we didn't set the standards, and they've already been cast in stone, we're going to have to use them. So I think the wisdom here is not to say that we've got to invent everything ourselves. The wisdom here is to know what 10% or 20% or 30% probably at most of the stuff we have to invent, and what we should go use that exists. We didn't invent PostScript, did we? We got a laser rider out of it. And we were the first out there with the laser rider.
cues.zh: 因为我们没有制定标准，而标准已经被定死了，我们就得采用它们。所以我认为这里的智慧不在于说我们必须自己发明一切。这里的智慧在于知道哪些是我们必须自己发明的——大概最多 10%、20% 或 30%——以及哪些应该去用现成的东西。PostScript 不是我们发明的，对吧？我们从中做出了激光打印机。而我们是第一个推出激光打印机的。

cues.en: I think this whole notion of being so proprietary in every facet of what we do has really hurt us. And again, the management and the vision that we had encouraged that. Encouraged people to go reinvent the wheel out there our own way. And yeah, it might be 10% better, but usually it ended up being about 50% worse because there's a lot of smart people that don't work at Apple II.
cues.zh: 我觉得，我们在做的每个环节都这么封闭，这真的害了我们。而且，我们当时的的管理和愿景还鼓励了这种做法，鼓励大家各自为政、重新发明轮子。是啊，可能能好上10%，但通常结果反而差了大约50%，因为有很多聪明人并不在Apple II工作。

cues.en: Well, the only other thing I'd like to add is that I think it's important that Apple will be perceived as different. Because if Apple just says, we're just like everybody else but better, that really doesn't say anything at all. Yeah. No, I don't think it's good that Apple's perceived as different. I think it's important that Apple's perceived as much better. And if being different is essential to doing that, then we have to do that. But if we could be much better without being different, that'd be fine with me. I want to be much better. I don't care about being different. We'll have to be different in some ways to be much better.
cues.zh: 我想补充的唯一一点是，我认为Apple被视为与众不同很重要。因为如果Apple只说“我们和大家一样，只是更好”，那根本说明不了什么。对。不，我不认为Apple被视为与众不同是好事。我认为重要的是Apple被视为好得多。如果与众不同对做到这一点必不可少，那我们就得这么做。但如果我们能不比众不同却好得多，那我也乐意。我想好得多，不在乎是否与众不同。在某些方面，我们得与众不同才能好得多。

cues.en: But that's that's the prize wouldn't you agree? It has to be a whole lot better before it's noticed and right it has to hold it has to be in some ways different It has to be a whole lot better Yes, good morning
cues.zh: 但那就是奖赏，你不同意吗？它必须先好上一大截才会被注意到，对吧？它必须保持，必须在某些方面与众不同，必须好上一大截。是的，早上好。

cues.en: You said in your opening ground rules that there were lots of holes, holes that Apple couldn't necessarily do themselves without this community. As a visionary, do you think you could spend a couple minutes either enumerating or talking about those holes? Sure. Much of the great leverage of using computers these days is using them not just for computationally intensive tasks,
cues.zh: 你在开场规则里说过有很多漏洞，这些漏洞是Apple没有这个社区就未必能自己补上的。作为一个有远见的人，你能不能花几分钟列举或谈谈这些漏洞？当然。如今使用电脑的巨大杠杆，很大程度上在于不只是把它们用于计算密集型任务，

cues.en: but using them as a window into communication intensive tasks, as you know. And never have I seen something more powerful than this computation combined with this network technology that we now have. So not only networks throughout an organization, but of course the wide area networks through the internet. And I just want to focus on something that's very close to my heart, which is
cues.zh: 而是如你所知，把它们当作通向通信密集型任务的窗口。我从未见过比这种计算与我们如今拥有的网络技术相结合更强大的东西。所以不仅是组织内部的网络，当然还有通过互联网的广域网。我只想聚焦一件我非常关心的事，那就是

cues.en: living in a high-speed networked world to get your job done every day. Now, how many of you manage your own storage on your computers? How many of you back up your computers as an example? How many of you have had a crash in the last, you know, three years, four years? Right. Okay. Let me describe the world I live in. About eight years ago,
cues.zh: 生活在一个高速网络化的世界里，每天把活儿干完。现在，你们有多少人在自己的电脑上管理自己的存储？举个例子，你们有多少人备份自己的电脑？你们有多少人在过去，比如说三年、四年内遇到过崩溃？对。好。让我描述一下我生活的世界。大约八年前，

cues.en: We had high-speed networking connected to our now obsolete next hardware running running next step at the time and Because we were using NFS we were able to take all of our personal data our home directories we call them off of our local machines and put them on a server and the software made that completely transparent and
cues.zh: 我们把高速网络连接到当时运行NeXTSTEP的现已过时的NeXT硬件上，因为我们用的是NFS，所以能够把所有个人数据，也就是我们称之为家目录的东西，从本地机器上拿走放到服务器上，而软件让这一切完全透明，并且

cues.en: Because the server had a lot of RAM on it, in some cases it was actually faster to get stuff from the server than it was to get stuff off your local hard disk because in some cases it would be cached in the RAM of the server if it was in popular use. But what was really remarkable was that the organization could hire a professional person to back up that server every night and could afford to spend a little bit more on that server so maybe it had redundant disk drives.
cues.zh: 因为服务器上有很多 RAM，在某些情况下，从服务器取东西实际上比从本地硬盘取还快，因为某些内容如果很常用，就会被缓存在服务器的 RAM 里。但真正了不起的是，这个组织可以雇一个专业人员每晚备份那台服务器，也能在那台服务器上多花一点钱，所以它可能有冗余磁盘驱动器。

cues.en: redundant power supplies. And you know, in the last seven years, you know how many times I have lost any personal data? Zero. Do you know how many times I've backed up my computer? Zero. I have computers at Apple, at Next, at Pixar, and at home. I walk up to any of them and log in as myself. It goes over the network, finds my home directory on the server,

cues.zh: 让现有的复杂应用快五到十倍，这意味着三个人真的可以第一天带着一个概念走进车库，六到九个月后带着产品进入市场。如今，我在我们这个行业里已经十年、十二年没见过这种事了。这让我非常、非常、非常兴奋。还有人说，好吧，它只能在 Macintosh 上运行，或者只能在

So I'll tell you right now. I'll give you an example. I get about 200 email messages a day. Sans all of the get-rich-quick ones from the internet. And I've been in that mode now for five, six, seven years. And I've used about every email to me.
cues.zh: 如果不是这样，我大可以花两千块钱去买一台 Apple II，何必自己造一台呢？我们并不是想创业，我们只是想拥有一台电脑。所以我现在就告诉你。我举个例子。我每天大概收到 200 封邮件，还不算网上那些一夜暴富的垃圾邮件。这种情况已经持续了五六年七年了。我几乎用遍了发给我的每一封邮件。

cues.en: is the most important app I use. And I've used every email system I know of out there, and I can tell you that the one on Next Step or Rhapsody is literally almost an order of magnitude better, more productive than anything else I know of. I mean, I walk around Apple, and they're using the worst mail system in the world at Apple. And I know we could like,
cues.zh: 是我用过的最重要的应用。我用过市面上所有知道的邮件系统，可以告诉你，Next Step 或 Rhapsody 上的那个简直好了将近一个数量级，生产力比其他任何我知道的都高。我的意思是，我在 Apple 里转一圈，他们用的却是世界上最糟糕的邮件系统。我知道只要给他们一个好用的邮件系统，

cues.en: improve the productivity inside Apple, 30% if we just give them a good email system. And so it's amazing to me that something as obvious as email is so broken out there. Netscape's is awful. I mean, everybody's is awful. And if something as obvious as email is so broken. And the other one I mentioned before, spreadsheets. If you used Improv or Quantrix for a week, you would go, how come?
cues.zh: 就能把 Apple 内部的生产力提高 30%。所以让我惊讶的是，像邮件这么显而易见的东西居然这么糟糕。Netscape 的很烂。我是说，每个人的都很烂。如果像邮件这么显而易见的东西都这么糟糕。还有我之前提到的另一个，电子表格。如果你用 Improv 或 Quantrix 一周，你会问，为什么

cues.en: This hasn't completely replaced Excel for 75% of the people out there. Yeah, there's 25% that'll still want Excel for good reasons. But for 75% of the people, why hasn't this replaced it? And there are no answers to these questions except let's go do it. And that's my attitude about this thing. The other thing I feel very, very, very strongly is it's incredibly stupid for Apple
cues.zh: 它还没有完全取代 Excel，对市面上 75% 的人来说？是啊，有 25% 的人出于充分的理由仍然想要 Excel。但对 75% 的人来说，为什么它还没取代 Excel？这些问题没有答案，除了“我们去干吧”。这就是我对这件事的态度。另一件我非常非常非常强烈感觉到的事是，Apple 落到这种境地——Apple 要赢，Microsoft 就必须输——这蠢得离谱。

cues.en: to get in a position where for Apple to win, Microsoft has to lose. That's really dumb. I mean, I don't expect the federal government to break up Microsoft for a lot of reasons, the least of which is the federal government's a monopoly. I mean, they're buddies. So, I just, Microsoft's a fact of life. They're like the air we breathe, you know? So, there were probably the better analogies like bottled water because you do have to buy it.
cues.zh: 那真是太蠢了。我是说，我不指望联邦政府去拆分 Microsoft，原因有很多，最不重要的一条是联邦政府自己就是个垄断者。我是说，他们是一伙的。所以，我就是觉得，Microsoft 是生活的一部分。他们就像我们呼吸的空气，你懂吧？所以，可能有更好的类比，比如瓶装水，因为你确实得花钱买。

cues.en: But nonetheless, Apple can win without having to have Microsoft lose. I firmly believe that. And hopefully, Microsoft will increasingly over time realize that that is the case and that Apple represents a quite profitable part of their business. And they seem to be coming around to that point of view.
cues.zh: 但尽管如此，苹果可以做到赢，而不必让微软输。我对此深信不疑。而且我希望，微软能随着时间的推移越来越认识到这一点，认识到苹果是他们业务中相当赚钱的一部分。他们似乎也正在接受这个观点。

cues.en: And there's been some alliances announced between Microsoft and Apple. So I think that I really, really strongly feel that setting Microsoft up as Satan and having a holy war against Microsoft would be exactly the wrong thing for Apple to do. There are so many opportunities out there where Apple can really have tremendous advantage and not have to go head to head with Microsoft, but really go right to the customers. Yes, back, middle.
cues.zh: 另外，微软和苹果之间已经宣布了一些合作联盟。所以我真的、非常强烈地认为，把微软塑造成撒旦、对微软发动一场圣战，对苹果来说恰恰是最错误的做法。外面有太多的机会，苹果完全可以获得巨大优势，而不必和微软正面硬刚，而是直接面向客户。好，后排那位。

cues.en: I was hoping that you would venture an opinion this morning on how you see the future evolution of the Macintosh compatible market. I think the Macintosh compatible. First of all, let me state my opinion on this. It's just my personal opinion. I believe Apple should license everything. With a few exceptions that I'll go into in a minute. But I think that Apple should get a fair price for it. And I think the clone setup, the way it was set up, was done really poorly.
cues.zh: 我希望您今天上午能谈谈您对 Macintosh 兼容机市场未来演变的看法。关于 Macintosh 兼容机——首先，让我表明我的观点。这只是我个人的看法。我认为苹果应该把所有东西都授权出去，只有少数几个例外，我稍后会讲到。但我认为苹果应该为此收取合理的价格。而且我认为当时的克隆机授权体系，也就是它当初的搭建方式，做得实在太糟糕了。

cues.en: three, four years ago. For one thing, Apple licenses the hardware designs and forces the clone makers to use them. That's stupid. Let the clone makers do their own hardware designs. Let them do whatever hardware they want. Right? Don't tie their hands. But then again, don't give away. I mean, if they want to OEM Apple hardware and pay extra for that, if they want to use Apple hardware, fine. But if they don't, let them design their own. And on the software, Apple should get a fair price based on volume.
cues.zh: 那是三四年前的事了。一方面，苹果授权的是硬件设计，并强迫克隆厂商使用这些设计。这很愚蠢。应该让克隆厂商自己做硬件设计，让他们想做什么样的硬件就做什么样的硬件，对吧？不要捆绑他们的手脚。但话又说回来，也不要白白送出去。我是说，如果他们想 OEM 苹果的硬件、为此支付额外费用，想用苹果的硬件，那没问题。但如果他们不想用，就让他们自己设计。至于软件方面，苹果应该根据出货量收取合理的价格。

cues.en: As an example, if I'm a clone maker, as you know, some of the low-end Macintoshs, whether they're compatibles or not, probably don't make much money. Matter of fact, you could even imagine they might lose money just to get people into the fold. And to offset those kinds of low margin products, you need some higher margin products at the high end. So if you're a clone maker, you think, wow, I think I'll give Apple 10 bucks for the software, and I'll go after the $5,000 Mac market. Well, that would be really stupid for Apple to do.
cues.zh: 举个例子，如果我是做克隆机的，你也知道，那些低端 Macintosh，不管是不是兼容机，可能都赚不了什么钱。事实上，你甚至可以想象它们可能会亏钱，只是为了把人拉进这个圈子。而要抵消这些低毛利产品，你需要在高端有一些高毛利产品。所以如果你是克隆机制造商，你会想，哇，我给 Apple 10 美元软件费，然后去攻 5000 美元的 Mac 市场。嗯，Apple 要是真这么做就太蠢了。

cues.en: Because this clone maker is just a leech. They're living off the fact that Apple's got this business model to not make much money at some levels and try to eat some back at the high level. And by just going after the high level and paying 10 bucks for the software, that wouldn't be fair. So you want people to pay more money if they're in lower volume. Because the only way they can get to higher volume is to make some of those medium and low priced clones too.
cues.zh: 因为这个克隆机制造商就是个吸血鬼。他们靠的是 Apple 的商业模式——在某些层级不赚什么钱，试图在高端赚回来。而只攻高端、付 10 美元软件费，那就不公平了。所以你要让量小的人付更多钱。因为他们想要达到更大的量，唯一的办法就是也做一些中低价的克隆机。

cues.en: and make less margin. And if they're doing that, then they ought to get a lower price across their whole range of products. So I've been advocating to eliminate the licensing of the hardware and let the clone makers do whatever they want and B, to raise the price or the royalty of the software to a reasonable level and make it a scale based on volume. And I think that's the right thing to do and some of the clone makers have been going ballistic over and it's incredibly stupid.
cues.zh: 并且接受更低的毛利。如果他们这么做，那他们就应该在整个产品线上拿到更低的价格。所以我一直在主张：第一，取消硬件授权，让克隆机制造商想怎么做就怎么做；第二，把软件的价格或版税提高到合理水平，并让它按销量分级。我认为这才是正确的做法，而一些克隆机制造商对此暴跳如雷，这真是蠢得离谱。

cues.en: I mean, I don't think they ought to pay more for Rhapsody as an example than they do for, you know, other modern operating systems to license. But that's not 10 or 20 or 30 bucks. So, and I think that's where we'll end up and I think everybody will be fine and I think the clone makers will have a much easier time and they won't have to deal with dealing with Apple's hardware and maybe they'll make some better hardware and maybe they'll make some worse hardware and the customers will decide. And I'm all for it.
cues.zh: 我是说，举例来说，我不认为他们为Rhapsody付的钱应该比他们为其他现代操作系统付的授权费更多。但那也不是10块、20块或30块。所以我觉得我们最终会走到那一步，我觉得大家都会没事，我觉得克隆机制造商的日子会好过得多，他们不用再应付苹果的硬件，也许他们会做出更好的硬件，也许他们会做出更差的硬件，由客户来决定。我完全支持。

cues.en: I just think Apple ought to get a little bit of value out of their software and not just have the clone makers picking off their high margin products and paying 10 bucks a copy. If they want to pick off the high margin products and pay a fair price for the software, let them have at it. So that's how I feel about that. But I'm not making the decisions. Yes? Even so, I'm glad you're here. Thanks. What's that? Even if you're not making decisions, thank you for being here. Oh, sure. You mentioned managing complexity.
cues.zh: 我只是觉得苹果应该从他们的软件中获得一点价值，而不是让克隆机制造商挑走他们的高利润产品，每份只付10块钱。如果他们想挑走高利润产品并为此支付公平的价格，那就让他们去做吧。这就是我对这件事的看法。但做决定的不是我。是吧？尽管如此，我很高兴你在这里。谢谢。什么？即使你不做决定，也谢谢你在这里。哦，当然。你提到了管理复杂性。

cues.en: There's a lot of people out there who are either not using computers or think of computers as something they have to babysit, that they work for their computers. How can we get computers to where they work for people instead? I don't really know. I mean, I'm not sure what you mean. I don't feel I work for my computer. I feel it's a little invasive. I mean, I have a T1 to my house and I... You sort of get in the habit of...
cues.zh: 有很多人要么不用电脑，要么把电脑看作是需要他们照看的东西，是他们在为电脑工作。我们怎么能让电脑为人们工作，而不是反过来？我真不知道。我是说，我不确定你指的是什么。我不觉得自己在为电脑工作。我觉得它有点侵入性。我是说，我家里有一条T1线路，而且我……你会养成一种习惯……

cues.en: of answering your email within a few seconds after it arrives so it can be invasive on a family life. I just think it can serve us more and go out and do things for us without us having to sort of watch. We have this whole system of, I click once, the computer does one thing, I click another thing, the computer does one thing, and it never goes out and works for me for 15 or 20 minutes. I mean, well, compiling.
cues.zh: 在邮件到达后几秒内就回复，这可能会侵扰家庭生活。我只是觉得，它可以为我们服务更多，替我们出去做事，而不需要我们一直盯着。我们有这么一整套系统：我点一下，电脑做一件事；我再点一下，电脑又做一件事，它从来不会自己出去替我工作个15、20分钟。我是说，嗯，编译就是这样的。

cues.en: I guess my point of view is a little different on that. My point of view is that I am routinely running 10 to 15 applications at once on my computer. They are all routinely talking to each other in a very wonderful way that I don't have to pay much attention to. And I can move things between them very easily. And I'm connected in an extremely high speed, easy, transparent, productive way with my colleagues. It's so much better
cues.zh: 我想我的观点在这方面有点不同。我的观点是，我通常会在电脑上同时运行10到15个应用。它们都以一种非常美妙的方式相互通信，而我不必太在意。我可以在它们之间轻松移动东西。而且我与同事之间以极高速、简便、透明、高效的方式保持联系。这比

cues.en: than anything I see in the Windows or the Mac world today. That I will be happy if over the next 12 to 24 months as you guys roll out your apps that we can just bring this to everybody. Secondly, I know there's at least 20 more apps that I'd love to be using that haven't been written yet. And if we can make those apps really easy to write and if we can keep the Mac market
cues.zh: 我今天在Windows或Mac世界里看到的任何东西都好得多。所以，如果未来12到24个月里，你们推出应用时，我们能把这个带给所有人，我会很高兴。其次，我知道至少还有20多个应用我很想用，但还没被写出来。如果我们能让那些应用真正容易编写，并且如果我们能让Mac市场的

cues.en: far less expensive to market into than the windtail market, so that you can get them to market, then we can all get a chance to use those great apps that you guys are going to write. So, my view is that for the next several years, like three, four years, our job is not to reinvent the world, it's to take something that we know exists already, but hardly anybody's got it, and get it out to them, you know?
cues.zh: 营销成本远低于Windows市场，这样你们就能把它们推向市场，那么我们都能有机会用上你们将要编写的那些出色应用。所以，我的观点是，在未来几年，比如三四年里，我们的工作不是重塑世界，而是拿出一些我们知道已经存在、但几乎没人拥有的东西，把它带给人们，你明白吗？

cues.en: And it's, to be honest, it's a lot like Xerox PARC. I mean, Xerox PARC had some of the things that were in a Macintosh, just nobody else had them. Well, there's thousands of people out there that use this now, but there aren't millions. And if we can get that out there, I think it's going to change a lot. And fortunately, a lot of it is tried and true and polished and refined, and it's pretty bulletproof. So we're not going to have to go through any embarrassing early moments, I hope. That would be cool. You mentioned tools.
cues.zh: 说实话，这很像 Xerox PARC。我是说，Xerox PARC 有一些后来出现在 Macintosh 里的东西，只是当时别人都没有。现在有成千上万人在用这个，但还不到数百万。如果我们能把它推广出去，我认为会带来很大改变。幸运的是，其中很多都经过实践检验、打磨完善，相当可靠。所以希望我们不会经历任何尴尬的早期阶段。那会很酷。你提到了工具。

cues.en: the, there is a, I noticed the great wonderful next step demo where we have a visual way of building the interface is great. And then all of a sudden we're back into text to do a little coding to add a few things. And there is already something that visually programs called program. And it's, it's probably a lost cause, but something like that has got to get here one day. And you know what? In the meantime, we'll go ahead and I'll do the next step. I'll do it. I'm doing it. Here's the deal.
cues.zh: 我注意到那个很棒的 next step 演示，我们可以用可视化的方式构建界面，这很好。但突然间我们又回到文本里去写点代码，加一些东西。而且已经有一个叫 program 的可视化编程工具了。它可能注定失败，但类似的东西总有一天得出现。你知道吗？在此期间，我们会继续推进，我来做下一步。我来做。我正在做。事情是这样的。

cues.en: The way you get programmer productivity is not by increasing the lines of code per programmer per day. That doesn't work. The way you get programmer productivity is by eliminating lines of code you have to write. The line of code that's the fastest to write, that never breaks, that doesn't need maintenance, is the line you never had to write.
cues.zh: 提升程序员生产力的方式，不是增加每个程序员每天写的代码行数。那行不通。提升程序员生产力的方式，是消除那些你不得不写的代码行。写起来最快、永不崩溃、无需维护的代码行，就是你从来不需要写的那一行。

cues.en: The goal here is to eliminate 80% of the code that you have to write for your app. That's the goal. And so along the way, if we can provide whizzy this and whizzy that and visual this and visual that, well, that's fine. But the high order bit is to eliminate 80% of the code. When you drag a line in Interface Builder, you're eliminating code of one form. But that only goes so far. Maybe we can go further.
cues.zh: 我们的目标是让你为应用编写的代码减少 80%。这就是目标。所以一路上，如果我们能提供些炫酷的功能、可视化功能之类的，那当然也不错。但最重要的是，让代码减少 80%。你在 Interface Builder 里拖一条线，就省去了某种形式的代码。但这还远远不够。也许我们还能做得更多。

cues.en: I've seen a lot of demos of things that try to take it all the way back into the algorithmic part of the code base, and none of them have ever been any good. If there are any good ones out there, show them to Avi, and he'll show them to me. Love to see him. Sir? Yeah, you mentioned how good it is that Apple controls the hardware, or at the very least that Apple controls something like Chirp, which is the hardware spec.
cues.zh: 我见过很多演示，试图把这一切彻底带回代码库的算法层面，但没有一个真正做得好。如果有好的例子，拿给 Avi 看，他会再拿给我看。我很乐意看看。先生？是的，你提到 Apple 控制硬件有多重要，或者至少 Apple 控制着像 Chirp 这样的东西，也就是硬件规格。

cues.en: And indeed, I hear really good things about it. I hear that Apple, or I hear that Chirp has really fast bus speeds. I heard they've really improved the I.O. subsystem. And then it came to the conference. I actually talked to some of the people working on it. And on the cloning side, I heard that Chirp is done. They've already finished the hardware. They're ready to go into production. I heard some people here at Apple working on the software side. And they said, well, that software side is actually done, too. It's all waiting on some weird negotiations going on with the cloners. And then there's rumor going on that
cues.zh: 确实，我听说这方面评价很高。我听说 Apple，或者说 Chirp，拥有非常快的总线速度。我还听说它们大幅改进了 I/O 子系统。后来我来到这次会议，和一些参与项目的人聊了聊。在克隆机这边，我听说 Chirp 已经完成了。他们已经做好了硬件，准备投产。我还听说 Apple 有些人在负责软件，他们说软件也已经完成了。一切都在等克隆机厂商之间一些奇怪的谈判。然后又有传言说……

cues.en: The reason that's caught up in negotiations is because Apple's concerned that the performance of trip is good enough that it's going to cannibalize some of their own markets. And it seems to me there's a conflict of interest here between Apple's own hardware and some of the cloning hardware where... Yeah, I don't believe that's true at all. I mean, the person running hardware at Apple, I have known for a decade. His name is John Rubenstein. I trust him with my life. He's the best...
cues.zh: 谈判之所以陷入僵局，是因为 Apple 担心 trip 的性能足够好，会蚕食自家的一些市场。我觉得这里 Apple 自己的硬件和某些克隆机硬件之间存在利益冲突……不，我完全不这么认为。我认识 Apple 硬件部门的负责人已经十年了。他叫 John Rubenstein，我愿意把性命托付给他。他是最优秀的……

cues.en: hardware leader I have ever seen in my life. He's really, really, really good. He comes from very high performance systems. And what his expertise is, is putting a lot of those high performance systems in silicon so they can be really cheap. Right? He's really good at that. He's really good at leading teams of very talented engineering managers and engineers. And what he wants to do is build some kick-ass stuff. Because the Mac hardware is not at the top of the food chain, let's just say.
cues.zh: 我见过的最厉害的硬件负责人。他真的非常非常出色。他来自高性能系统领域。他的专长是把很多高性能系统做成芯片，从而大幅降低成本。对吧？他非常擅长这个。他也很擅长带领由优秀工程经理和工程师组成的团队。他想做的是打造一些超牛的东西。因为 Mac 硬件并不是食物链顶端，这么说吧。

cues.en: And we want to get it there. And we are going to get it there. So if there was something ready to go that was really good, I promise you, John would be shipping it yesterday. And in terms of the clone makers, I know that what John is pushing for very strongly, which I support 100%, is to tell the clone makers they can build their own hardware. That's the easiest thing to do. Don't be limited by what Apple does or does not release. Build your own.
cues.zh: 我们想让它登顶。而且我们一定会做到。所以如果有真正好且ready to go的东西，我向你保证，John 昨天就会发货了。至于克隆厂商，我知道 John 强烈主张、我也百分百支持的，就是告诉克隆厂商他们可以自己造硬件。这是最简单的事。不要被 Apple 发布或不发布什么限制住。自己造。

cues.en: There's a billion people out there building hardware. Look at the PC clone business. They all build their own hardware. They could have people build it for them. cues.zh: 我不认为世界的重点是把我的生活放在这个小东西上，等我回到基站时再红外同步到电脑里。我觉得，对我来说，我想要的是随身带的这个小东西，上面有键盘。因为如果你做邮件，你需要键盘，直到语音识别完美为止。你需要键盘。你不会坐在那儿手写。你需要键盘。而且你需要连上网。所以如果有人能做出一个小东西，
